content.text: Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, similar sub-problems. Each time the function calls itself, it works with a simpler version of the original problem, getting closer to a basic case that doesn't need recursion. The function must have a "base case"—a condition where it stops calling itself and returns a direct answer—otherwise it would call itself forever. Once the base case is reached, each function call returns its result back up the chain, combining all the answers to solve the original problem.
